statement.p: For the figures below, determine the nature of \displaystyle \lim_{x\to a}\,\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}, if f(x) is shown as the blue curve and g(x) as the black curve.

image.shortdescription: Graph of two functions with value 0 when x=a
image.description: a blue line with positive slope passing through (a,0), and a black line with negative slope passing through (a,0).

image.shortdescription: Graph of two functions with value 0 when x=a
image.description: a blue line with a large negative slope passing through (a,0), and a black parabola opening downward with vertex (a,0).

solution.p: In either case, we use l'Hopital's rule, \lim_{x\to a} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{f'(a)}{g'(a)}.
For the left graph, since f'(a) > 0 and g'(a) \lt 0, the limit is negative..
For the right graph, since f'(a) \ne 0 and g'(a) = 0, the limit is undefined..
